title: Token Signal Atlas: journey mapping & wireframe notes (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures an exploratory UX approach for surfacing token-level signals (cost + latency + quality proxies) within Console. The goal is to produce a wireframe and backlog-ready checklist for a first prototype: the Token Signal Atlas — a single-pane investigator for per-invocation forensic and aggregate analysis.

Background & problem statement:
- Customers need to troubleshoot surprising unit-cost spikes and tail latency regressions at the granularity of individual tokens (not just per-invocation averages).
- Current Console views expose per-invocation metrics and model-level aggregates but lack a compact way to trace which tokens (prefix/content/system) drive cost/latency and how model routing, batching, and caching contribute.
- Hypothesis: a combined timeline + per-token heatstrip + failure-mode annotations will let engineers quickly surface root causes and iterate on batching/caching policies or prompt edits.

Key user personas (primary focus):
- Backend engineer debugging an 99th-percentile latency spike after a model rollout.
- ML infra engineer validating the effect of a quantization profile on token decode cost.
- Product engineer evaluating per-invocation cost regressions across two model variants.

Signal taxonomy (for wireframe labels):
- Token cost (unit tokens*per-token-price) — derived from token length * model-rate and adjusted by cached-prefix hits.
- Decode time — time spent in model decode per token (ms).
- KV prefix hit/miss — boolean signal; important for cache-driven cost anomalies.
- Batch-wait time — time a request waited in batching queue before execution (ms).
- External-call cost/time — e.g., tool calls or grounding API latencies attributed to token spans.
- Quality flags (proxied) — early-stopping, truncated, repetition-rate (simple heuristics).

Wireframe components (left-to-right flow):
1) Top filter bar: time range, model variant selector, route, customer-tier, cost threshold slider, latency percentile selector.
2) Investigator canvas: large timeline with stacked small-multiples: overall tokens/sec, average token cost, p95/p99 decode time. Zoom controls.
3) Heatstrip lane (per-invocation compact): horizontal strip where each char/bin represents token buckets; color = unit-cost intensity, border = kv cache miss, glow = external-call span. Hover reveals token text, token index, cost delta. Click expands invocation.
4) Invocation detail panel (right side): full prompt + response with inline token annotations: per-token cost, ms, batch wait, cache status, quality flags. Buttons: annotate-save (adds to eval set), pin-invocation, open-in-replay (links to replay tool).
5) Compare mode overlay: select up to 2 invocations or 2 model variants and show diff heatstrip (green = lower cost/latency, red = worse).
6) Failure-mode timeline: below canvas, shows annotations for rollout events, autoscaler bursts, quantization flips, deployment fallbacks.

Interaction notes & micro-behaviors:
- Hover microcard must show token-level context and breadcrumb to trace origin (system/prompt/user/content).
- When multiple invocations selected, show aggregated per-token percentile bands (median + p90 ribbon).
- Allow toggle: token-aligned view vs. time-aligned view (helpful for comparing batching effects).
- Persist selected invocation as a URL hash for sharing with SRE/SE.

Example investigative flows (scenarios):
A) Batch spike: infra engineer sees p99 decode jump after a traffic surge. Filter to p99, open timeline, heatstrip shows longer batch-wait times aligned with large tokens. Outcome: adjust batching policy or add request- size guard. Linked hypothesis JIRA-CORE-3127.
B) Cache regression: product engineer sees cost increase only for one customer route. Heatstrip shows previously-cached prefix now flagged miss; invocation detail shows client prompt changed slightly (whitespace/tokenization). Outcome: propose advice in SDK to normalize prompt formatting; QA to regenerate cache key.
C) Tool call amplification: some tokens glow (external-call); invocation detail shows repeated tool calls for the same span. Outcome: recommend dedupe or change prompt to reduce tool calls.

Wireframe annotations for designers:
- Heatstrip color scale must be perceptually uniform; consider log scale for cost.
- Token glyph width: variable with scaled binning (not literal glyph widths) to fit long responses — hover to expand.
- Mobile: fall back to single-invocation view and compact histogram (no heatstrip).
- Keyboard nav: left/right to move token cursor, space to pin.

Backlog & next steps (prioritized):
- UX spike: interactive prototype (Figma) for heatstrip + detail panel (owner: Hannah) — ETA 2w — JIRA-UX-798.
- Instrumentation work: emit per-token decode_time + kv_hit events in trace-level export (owner: Omar) — spike + perf cost estimate — JIRA-ENG-1122.
- API: endpoint to fetch invocation token map and annotations (owner: Benito) — add to API backlog.
- Small rollout: internal-only feature flag behind org-level toggle, start with 10 customers.

Open questions / risks:
- Privacy: do we store raw tokens in Console logs? Need alignment with security on retention and redaction (security contact: Sasha Kramer).
- Cost of storing per-token telemetry at scale — need sampling strategy (store full token maps for pinned/p99 invocations; sampled otherwise).
- Performance: rendering heatstrips for high-throughput timelines needs virtualization. Consider server-side aggregation.

Prototype acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Designer prototype + clickthrough demonstrating hover/expand behaviors.
- Instrumentation exists to compute per-token cost + decode_time for a sample window.
- Console can display and share a pinned invocation URL with annotations.
- 3 engineering/regression playbooks written for the top 3 failure modes (batching, cache, tool-amplification).

Quick notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally sketches a combined investigator + summary canvas instead of a separate per-invocation page; reasoning: many root causes only reveal themselves when you see distribution + exemplar invocations together.
- Please flag any privacy or retention blockers ASAP.

References & seeds for design team:
- Existing per-invocation detail pattern: /product/console-and-rollouts/per-invocation-econ-ux-journey-and-wires.json (use for behavioral parity).
- Data infra ticket: JIRA-CORE-3127 (sampling + schema).

Action items (this week):
- Hannah: initial figma frames for heatstrip + detail panel (due 2024-09-24).
- Omar: short spike to confirm trace event shape (due 2024-09-20).
- Priya: draft rollout plan and customer comms template for internal review (due 2024-09-27).

Notes-to-self (short):
- Consider adding a small 'why-this-matters' snippet in top-left to help new users.
- Think about a compact export to CSV for billing analysis (per-invocation token costs aggregated by route).
